newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver closes lower, gold stays steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver closes lower, gold stays steady.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) closes 40 rupees lower at 6,800 rupees per kg, recovering only marginally by five rupees over its opening of 6,795 rupees per kg. It lost 55 rupees per kg on Monday.
** Gold 24 carats stays steady to end at 4,680 rupees per kg, with traders reporting poor activity. Gold last gained 10 rupees per 10 grammes on Friday.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) close unchanged at 54,800 rupees per piece.
Silver (.999) closed 45 rupees lower at 6,800 rupees on Tuesday on a weak international trend, dealers said.
"The market is under some psychological impact. There was not much selling," said a dealer. On Monday silver closed 55 rupees lower at 6,840 rupees per kg.
Gold remained steady for the third day in a row at 4,680 rupees per 10 grammes. The price of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) ended unchanged at 54,800 rupees per piece.
"The market will move only if there are fluctuations in global prices, but not due to local demand, which is not there," said Bombay Bullion Association president M.L.Damani.
Dealers attributed the lack of demand for both gold and silver to the slack period that sets in at the end of the traditional wedding season in May. (Conversion $1=35.77 rupees)
